findings.code_snippet:
## Loopback Relay Variant

Use this variant when the relay runs on this machine. Discovery is `GET https://127.0.0.1<sni-port>/api/state` and the service is `https://<name>.localhost:<sni-port>/`. `*.localhost` usually resolves to `::1` first, and a development relay often has a self-signed certificate, so probe with `curl -sk --ipv4 --connect-timeout 5 --max-time 15`. Read `-k` as a development-only concession and say so in the handoff.

findings.code_snippet:
`portal expose` defaults `--identity-path` to `identity.json` in the process working directory. That file is created automatically and contains private key material. Always pass an absolute path outside the repository. The `IDENTITY_PATH` environment variable sets the same flag, and the same variable name means the identity directory for `relay-server`; on a host that runs both, prefer the explicit flag.

An existing identity file supplies the saved public name as well as the key. `--name` applies only when a new identity is created and never renames an existing one, so use one identity file per public name.

findings.code_snippet:
## Secret handling

- `portal expose` defaults `--identity-path` to `./identity.json` and writes `private_key`, `mnemonic`, and `token_secret` there. Always override it with an absolute path outside the repository. For `portal agent`, omit `identity_path` so identity stays under the agent state directory.
- Never print or commit Portal identity JSON, private keys, access tokens, agent endpoint tokens, wallet material, payment facilitator tokens, installer credentials, OIDC client secrets, identity proofs (`AUTH_IDENTITY_PROOF`), or credential links issued by `portal auth issue` (a credential is a bearer token for the app). The one exception is handing a redeem URL, once, to the user who asked for it, as `application-auth.md` describes; a client secret is written to a file only as the persistent-agent section there describes.
- Keep persistent identity and agent state outside the repository. If the user intentionally keeps state under the project, verify that its directory is ignored be
findings.message: Code accesses credential files (SSH keys, AWS credentials, etc.). This could indicate credential theft attempts.
findings.remediation: Remove references to credential paths. Use environment variables or secrets managers. For docs, use placeholder paths (e.g., /path/to/config). Never load .env or token files in production code paths.

e agent does not read the `AUTH_OIDC_*` variables and has no way to refer to a secret, so a client secret can only be stored in the TOML file as plain text. Tell the user so, and store it only after they explicitly accept that risk (the rule is in `references/safety-and-verification.md`). If they do not, the user runs the tunnel with `portal expose` from their own terminal, as step 5 of the oidc section describes.

When they accept, first make the config file private, before any secret exists: `chmod 600 <config>`, and check that its folder is not open to other users. A new file takes the user's umask, often `0644`. A recent agent clears the group and other permissions itself before it stores a secret (on Windows it checks the file's ACL), but an older one writes the file with the mode it already has, so a `0644` file would hold the secret readable by everyone from the moment it is saved, and a file you write by hand is never tightened. findings.message: Skill establishes unauthorized persistence across sessions via cron jobs, startup scripts, or state files. Session persistence allows an attacker to maintain access beyond the current interaction.
findings.remediation: Remove any persistence mechanisms (cron jobs, startup scripts, state files). Skills should not maintain state across sessions without explicit user consent.

findings.code_snippet:
## Persistent agent

`portal agent run` without `--foreground` installs and starts a per-user OS service (launchd LaunchAgent or systemd user unit). Obtain approval before that path. `--foreground` keeps the agent in the current process and skips service installation.

`run`, `restart`, and `stop` are service-wide. They apply to every `[[tunnels]]` entry owned by that `service_name`. Do not point a second config at the default `portal-agent` service if an existing agent already has unrelated tunnels. An isolated agent also needs its own `state_dir` and loopback `control_addr`; those otherwise default to the shared data directory and `127.0.0.1:4018`.
